title: Hybrid FlashAttention v3 integration and prefill-decode pacing experiments
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Background: FlashAttention v3 (FAv3) offers new memory layout and kernel fusion improvements that increase raw token throughput on long sequences, but our early internal trials surfaced higher tail latency for small-batch decode workloads and intermittent OOMs on mixed-size request streams. Goal: produce a safe rollout plan to integrate FAv3 into the runtime with a hybrid kernel planner that chooses FAv3/FAv2/legacy kernels by workload shape and node state, and implement prefill->decode pacing heuristics to avoid KV-cache churn and decode stalls. This ticket covers design, microbenchmarks, autotuner extension, canary rollout, and regression detection hooks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hybrid kernel planner implemented and behind config flag. 2) Automated microbench suite (seq lengths 32/128/512/1024, batch sizes 1..32) added to perf CI with baseline vs FAv2/FAv3. 3) Canary rollout that routes 5% of traffic to FAv3 path with automatic fallback on latency/oom signals. 4) Prefill-decode pacing heuristics deployed and verified to reduce OOM and tail-latency spikes on mixed workloads. 5) Documentation for operators (console flag, observability metrics, rollback steps).
steps: Design hybrid kernel planner: heuristics + lookup table + online metric feedback
Extend autotuner to capture per-kernel memory margin and occupancy on target GPU families (A100/H100)
Implement prefill->decode pacing window to enforce gradual prefill weight distribution and KV cache warming
Add microbench harness and GPU perf job (seq x batch sweep) in CI infra
Run lab experiments on A100 and H100; collect latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, GPU mem headroom, OOM count
Implement canary gateway routing and fallback triggers (oom, >30% increase in P95 vs baseline, GPU mem usage spike thresholds)
Observability: add metric labels kernel_variant, kernel_reason, prefill_pacing_token_rate and dashboard panels
Canary for production: 5% traffic for 48h, monitor and analyze; escalate to 20% if stable; manual rollback path documented
findings: Initial lab runs (H100, batch sizes 1..8): FAv3 gives +9-14% tokens/sec for seq>=512 vs FAv2 and reduces GPU occupancy by ~6% due to kernel fusion, but P95 latency regressed by up to 35% for batchsize=1 seq=128 under mixed request interleaving. On A100 the throughput wins are smaller (~4-7%) but memory margin is tighter leading to 2 observed OOMs during stress tests when prefill bursts align across workers. Prefill-decode pacing reduced OOMs to 0 in stress workloads and a tuned pacing window recovered P95 latency to within 10% of baseline while preserving ~7% throughput gain for long-seq flows.
decisions: Adopt hybrid planner by default behind runtime flag runtime.kernel.hybrid_fav3_enabled=false
Use FAv3 for sequences >= 512 when batch_size >= 4 on H100; otherwise prefer FAv2/legacy kernels
Introduce a dynamic memory margin heuristic: kernel selection requires estimated peak_memory + margin_pct (default 12%) to be available
Implement prefill pacing with default token_rate cap 2x steady-state decode rate and adaptive backoff on mem pressure
Canary strategy: start at 5% traffic for 48h, auto-fallback on 3 consecutive OOMs or P95 > baseline*1.3 over 15min window
risks: Risk of unseen regressions on uncommon model shapes (sparse attention or models with large KV projections). Operator complexity increases due to additional flags and metrics. Incorrect memory estimation can still cause OOMs during simultaneous prefill storms. Canary thresholds may need tuning per-customer fleet. There is also a small risk FAv3 kernel introduces numerical differences that subtly affect deterministic evals; we need regression checks in eval harness.
